In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah al-Balad

It is Meccan.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Nay, I swear by this city﴾. Its meaning: "I swear", and "lā" is a supplementary (ṣila) particle.

Al-Farrā' said: This is in accordance with the manner of Arabic speech, where they say: "No, by Allah, I will not do such-and-such" (lā wallāhi lā af'alu kadhā), meaning: "By Allah". Likewise: "No, by Allah, I will surely do such-and-such", meaning: "By Allah". So it is permissible that "lā" be a supplementary particle, and it is permissible that it be a reply to a previous statement, with the oath beginning from the words "by Allah". Similarly, His words ﴿Nay, I swear﴾ may be understood with "lā" as a supplementary particle, or as a reply to their claim of denying the Resurrection or denying the prophethood of the Messenger, with the oath beginning from His words ﴿I swear﴾. Al-Farrā' said: This second view is preferable.

As for His words ﴿by this city﴾, it refers to Mecca according to all scholars, as related by Mujāhid, Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, Qatādah and others.

And His saying: ﴿And you are a resident of this city﴾ has three interpretations. The first: that is, it is lawful (ḥalāl) for you to fight in this city, which was not lawful for anyone before you. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Makkah is sacred; God made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth. It was not made lawful for anyone before me, and it will not be made lawful for anyone after me, and it was only made lawful for me for an hour of the day."

The second interpretation: His saying ﴿And you are a resident of this city﴾ means: they make lawful from you what God has forbidden, namely harm and inflicting what is disliked upon you, while believing in the sanctity of the Sacred Precinct (ḥaram). This is mentioned by al-Qaffāl.

The third interpretation: ﴿And you are a resident of this city﴾ means: you are dwelling in this city. This is an indication of the increase in the sanctity and honour of the city because of the presence of the Prophet in it.

And His saying: ﴿and by the begetter and what he begets﴾. Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Salih said its meaning is: Adam and his offspring. And from Abu 'Imran [al-Jawni]: it is Ibrahim and his offspring.

And 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that His saying: ﴿and the begetter and what he begets﴾ refers to the one who begets and the one who does not beget (the barren one), so that "ma" (what) is for negation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 90, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We created man in toil.﴾ Upon this the oath was made, (and the meaning of the oath is) and the meaning of kabad (toil) is: hardship.

Sharik narrated from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAlī, concerning His saying: ﴿and a father and what he begot﴾, that it refers to Adam and his offspring, according to what we have mentioned.

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu Muhammad al-Sarifini informed us of this, Abu al-Qasim ibn Hababa informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us, ʿAlī ibn al-Ja'd informed us, from Sharik... the report.

As for kabad, we have made clear that it means hardship.

ʿAlī ibn al-Ja'd narrated, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAlī al-Rifāʿī, from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, who said: No one struggles with hardship as much as the human being does.

Saʿīd said, "Khalaqnā al-insāna fī kabad" meaning: in the narrowness of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter.

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: We were informed of what we have mentioned from al-Ḥasan: al-Sarifini, from [Ibn] Hababa, from al-Baghawi, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ja'd.

It has been said in explanation of kabad: it is that he struggles with the narrowness of the womb, the difficulty of exiting the mother's belly, then he is in swaddling and wrapping, then the teething, then circumcision, then when he reaches the obligations, commands and prohibitions, then he struggles with the matter of his livelihood and the circumstances that turn against him until he dies, then after that what returns to the terrors of the grave and the terrors of the Resurrection, until he settles in one of the two abodes.

And Labid said about kabad:

﴿O eye, why do you not weep for Arbad, when we rose and the adversaries rose in kabad﴾

Meaning: in hardship.

Ibrahim, Mujahid and ʿAbdullah ibn Shaddad said: fī kabad means in uprightness, and the meaning is: that he was created upright in his mother's belly, not lying prone on his face, unlike the rest of the animals.

In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: that Allah the Exalted appointed an angel over the child in the mother's womb; when the woman stands up or lies down, he raises the child's head so that it does not drown in the blood.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 90, verse 5:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Does he think that no one will ever have power over him?﴾ The verse was revealed concerning Abu al-Ashaddayn (Abu al-Ashaddayn), who was a man from the Banu Jumah, among the strongest and most powerful of the Quraysh. A leather mat from ʿUkaz (ʿUkaẓ) would be spread out for him, and he would stand upon it, and the people would gather around the mat and pull it from under his feet, yet it would tear and his feet would not move. He was fierce in his enmity toward the Prophet (ﷺ), so God the Most High revealed this verse concerning him.

Its meaning: Does he suppose that God will never have power over him? He said this because he was deluded by his strength and might.

And His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance."﴾ That is: I spent much wealth in enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ). "Lubadan" means piled one upon another.

Al-Kalbi said: "And he was lying in that claim,

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Does he think that no one sees him?﴾ Does he think that Allah does not see what he spent? It is also said: Does he think that Allah has not been informed of his deed, so that he lies and Allah does not know his lie?

Ma'mar said: This verse was recited in the presence of Qatadah, and he said: Does he think that Allah the Exalted will not ask him where he gathered it from and where he spent it?

And on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: What did you do with your wealth? He will say: I spent it and gave zakah, seeking Your pleasure. He will be told: You lie. You spent only so that it would be said: So-and-so is generous, and that has been said. Then he will be dragged to the Fire."

The report is lengthy, authentic, and was narrated by Muslim.

It is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The feet of the son of Adam will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is questioned about four things: about his life, how he spent it; about his body, how he wore it out; about his wealth, from where he acquired it and where he spent it."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did We not make for him two eyes?﴾ The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: Then Allah the Exalted mentioned His blessings upon him and His great power, so that he would know that Allah is able to restore him on the Day of Resurrection as a new creation, and that he will be held accountable for what he does.
"And His saying: ﴿And a tongue and two lips﴾ — its meaning is apparent."

And His saying: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: the path of good and the path of evil.

And ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that His saying ﴿and We guided him to the two highways﴾ means: the two hands.

The first opinion is more well known, and it is the view of most of the commentators (mufassirun).

It has also been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "They are only two highways: the highway of good and the highway of evil, so do not make the highway of evil more beloved to you than the highway of good."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 90, verses 12–13:

And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the steep path is?﴾, meaning: what will make you know what (it is to) cross over the steep path? Then He explained it, saying: ﴿It is the freeing of a neck﴾. And freeing a neck is manumitting it.

It is narrated from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever frees a neck, it will be his ransom from the Fire."

It is well known that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, teach me a deed that will admit me to Paradise." He said: "If you have shortened the sermon, you have broadened the request. Free the nasamah (a soul), and free the neck." He said: "Are they not one and the same, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No. Freeing the nasamah means that you alone bear its emancipation, while freeing the neck means that you help with its price. And there is for you the shelter (fay') of kinship toward the wronging relative. If you cannot do that, then feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. And if you cannot do that, then restrain your tongue except for good."

It is also related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever frees a believing neck, Allah will free for every limb of it a limb of his from the Fire."

The report is sound.

It has been recited as "fakku raqabatin" (فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ). Whoever reads it in the nominative (raf') means: "it is the freeing of a neck." Whoever reads it in the accusative (naṣb) means: "He does not cross over the steep path except one who frees a neck."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 90, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger﴾, meaning: feeding a poor man on a day of hunger. Al-saghb (ّ) is hunger, and al-masghaba is famine.

The poet said:

(Had you been a neighbour, O son of Qays ibn 'Asim... I would not have spent the night full while your neighbour was hungry.)

Meaning: sagh'ib (hungry).

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿an orphan of near relationship﴾, meaning: one who is a relative. The orphan (yatim) is the one who has no father. It is also said: he is the one who has neither of his two parents.

Qays ibn al-Mulawwah said:

(I complain to God of the loss of Layla, as the orphan complains to God of the loss of his two parents.)

"And His saying: ﴿or a needy person in misery﴾, i.e., one pressed down into the dust by poverty.

Mujahid said: nothing stands between him and the dust.

It is also said: ﴿dhā matraba﴾ means one afflicted by a debilitating illness (zamāna), and it is also said: ﴿dhā matraba﴾ means one who has no one among the people (to help him)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 90, verse 17:

And His saying: ﴿Then he was among those who believed﴾ means: he who ventures upon the steep path (al-'aqabah) by doing these things, then he was among those who believed.

If it is said: the word "thumma" (then) indicates a delay (tarakhi) by the agreement of the scholars of the language, so how is the meaning of the verse to be understood, since faith is mentioned as being delayed after these deeds?

The answer: al-Nahhas said: "It is problematic, and the best that has been said about it is that its meaning is: then I inform you that he was among those who believed at the time he did these things." It has also been said that "thumma" here carries the sense of "wa" (and), but this is not sound.

And His saying: ﴿and enjoined one another to patience﴾ means: to patience in refraining from the disobedience of Allah. It has also been said: to patience in obedience to Allah, and it has been said: to patience in refraining from the pleasures of this world and its desires.

And His saying: ﴿and enjoined one another to compassion﴾ means: the compassion of some of them toward others, and "enjoining one another to compassion" is the charge of one to another.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Those are the companions of the right hand﴾, meaning: the people of the right (ashab al-yamin), who are those who were brought out from the right side of Adam. It is also said: those who are given the Book in their right hands. And it has been said: the blessed ones (al-mayamin) with respect to themselves.

And His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve in Our signs, they are the companions of the left hand﴾. That is: the people of misfortune (al-mashā'īm) upon themselves. And it is said: they are those who are given their book in their left hand. And likewise the first statement.

And His saying: ﴿Upon them will be a fire, closed in﴾ — meaning sealed shut, enclosed. It is said: "wassadtu al-bab" and "aṣdatu" when one shuts the door, i.e., closes it tightly. It is also said: "mu'sada," meaning "mubhama," having no door at all.

The poet said:

(A people who reconcile the severity of their sons' ... and chains, links, and a door sealed shut)

That is, "mutbaqan" (closed tight).
